mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns remain negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and increasing S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate falls below 3.5%, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: When both industrial production and housing starts increase, it indicates strong economic activity, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both industrial production and housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative over 60 days in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Federal funds rate exceeds 5%, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Consumer Price Index indicates inflation, leading to potential rate hikes and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: CPI increases by more than 0.5% in a month, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in retail sales signals strong consumer demand, leading to higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth exceeds 5%, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high employment levels indicate a strong economy, leading to increased S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment is below 4% and employment is high, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, slowing industrial production indicates reduced economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is below 2%, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
